child abuse or domestic abuse is received and continues through the initial clinical assessment. The FAP case manager requests information from a variety of sources, in addition to the victim and the abuser (whether alleged or adjudicated), to identify abusive risk factors and to clarify the context of the use of violence, and ascertain the level of risk and the lethality using standardized instruments.

(i) III PS 71: Ongoing risk assessment. (a) A FAP risk assessment is conducted from the clinical assessment until the case closes.

(ii) During each contact with the victim;

(iii) During each contact with the abuser (whether alleged or adjudicated);

(iv) Whenever the abuser is alleged to have committed a new incident of child abuse or domestic abuse;

(v) During significant transition periods for the victim or abuser;

(vi) When destabilizing events for the victim or abuser occur; or

(vii) When clinically relevant issues are uncovered during clinical intervention services.

(viii) The FAP case manager monitors risk at least quarterly when civilian agencies provide the clinical intervention services or conducts risk assessments through MOU with agencies.

(ix) The FAP case manager monitors risk at least monthly when the victim is high risk or involves chronic child neglect or child sexual abuse.

(x) PS 72: Communication of increased risk. The FAP communicates in cases of risk or risk to lethality of the appropriate commanders, law enforcement, or civilian officials. FAP clinical staff assess whether the increased risk requires the victim to advocate to be urged to review the victim's safety plan.

(5) Clinical assessment. (a) PS 72: Clinical assessment policy. The installation FAP establishes procedures for the prompt clinical assessment of victims, abusers (whether alleged or adjudicated), and other family members, who are eligible to receive treatment in a military medical facility, in reports of child abuse and unrestricted reports of domestic abuse in accord with subpart A of this part and DoD 6025.18-R when applicable and Service FAP headquarters policies and guidance, including:

(A) A prompt response based on the severity of the alleged abuse and further abuse;

(B) Developmentally appropriate clinical tools and measures to be used, including those that take into account relevant cultural attitudes and practices;

(C) Timelines for FAP staff to complete the assessment of an alleged incident;

(D) The nature of the information being sought;

(E) The sources from which information will be sought;

(F) The reasons why the information is being sought;

(G) The circumstances in accordance with 10 U.S.C. 552a, DoD 6025.18-R, 32 CFR part 310, and Service FAP headquarters policies and guidance under which the information may be released to others;

(H) The procedures under 5 U.S.C. 552a, DoD 6025.18-R, 32 CFR part 310, and Service FAP headquarters policies and guidance for requesting the authorization for such information.

(I) The procedures under 5 U.S.C. 552a, DoD 6025.18-R, 32 CFR part 310, and Service FAP headquarters policies and guidance by which a person may request access to his or her record.
